title: Yesterday — the past tense, which is actually easier
goal: Talk about what already happened — and discover that the part of Persian learners fear most is in fact its most regular.
bekal: form a past-tense sentence from any verb without memorizing anything
tell about trips, events, and experiences

dialogs.title: گفتگو — سفرِ شیراز
dialogs.intro: Budi has just come back from a four-day trip to Shiraz. Maryam wants to hear all about it.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: عالی بود! پنج‌شنبه با اتوبوس رفتم.
lines.baca: âli bud! panj-shanbe bâ otobus raftam.
lines.id: Amazing! I left by bus on Thursday.
lines.literal: amazing was! Thursday with bus went-I.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: Twelve hours! Didn't you get tired?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: نه، خوابیدم. صبح رسیدم و مستقیم به آرامگاهِ حافظ رفتم.
lines.baca: na, khâbidam. sobh residam va mostaghim be ârâmgâh-e Hâfez raftam.
lines.id: No, I slept. I arrived in the morning and went straight to Hafez's tomb.
lines.literal: no, slept-I. morning arrived-I and straight to tomb-of Hafez went-I.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: بله! یک پیرمرد شعر را برایم خواند و معنی‌اش را گفت.
lines.baca: bale! yek pirmard she'r râ barâyam khând va ma'niyash râ goft.
lines.id: Yes! An old man read me the poem and explained what it meant.
lines.literal: yes! one old-man poem [obj] for-me read-he and meaning-its [obj] said-he.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: گفت سفرِ من به نتیجهٔ خوبی می‌رسد. خوشحال شدم.
lines.baca: goft safar-e man be natije-ye khubi miresad. khoshhâl shodam.
lines.id: He said my trip would end well. I was happy.
lines.literal: said-he trip-of I to result-of good-a arrives-it. happy became-I.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: Did you go to Persepolis too?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: بله، جمعه. با تاکسی رفتیم و چهار ساعت آنجا ماندیم.
lines.baca: bale, jom'e. bâ tâksi raftim va chahâr sâ'at ânjâ mândim.
lines.id: Yes, on Friday. We went by taxi and stayed there four hours.
lines.literal: yes, Friday. with taxi went-we and four hour there stayed-we.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: صد تا! ولی گوشی‌ام شب باتری نداشت.
lines.baca: sad tâ! vali gushi-am shab bâtri nadâsht.
lines.id: A hundred! But by evening my phone's battery was dead.
lines.literal: hundred piece! but phone-my evening battery not-had-it.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: What did you have for dinner?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: کبابِ شیرازی. خیلی خوشمزه بود. غذایِ تند نبود!
lines.baca: kabâb-e shirâzi. kheyli khoshmaze bud. ghazâ-ye tond nabud!
lines.id: Shirazi kebab. It was delicious. And it wasn't spicy!
lines.literal: kebab-of Shirazi. very tasty was. food-of spicy not-was!

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: I told you so! Isfahan next time.

notes: **Past stem = infinitive minus ـن. Without a single exception.** رفتن → رفت، خوردن → خورد، دیدن → دید، گفتن → گفت، ماندن → ماند. Compare the present stems in unit 9, which had to be memorized one by one — here you just cut off one letter and you're always right.

⚠️ **The او form takes no ending at all.** رفت ("he/she went"), گفت ("he/she said"), خواند ("he/she read"). This is the only place in all of Persian where the person ending is empty, and that actually makes it easy to spot: if a past verb ends with no ending, the subject is "he/she".
**The verb بود is the past of بودن ("to be").** بودم، بودی، بود، بودیم، بودید، بودند. Negative: نبود. It replaces است in past sentences: خوب است ("it's good") → خوب بود ("it was good").
**Past tense of داشتن is regular too:** داشتم، داشتی، داشت، داشتیم، داشتید، داشتند. Negative: نداشت. Notice that داشتن — odd in the present because it takes no می — is completely normal in the past.
**"I told you so" = گفته بودم** uses a form you haven't learned yet (ماضی بعید, the past perfect). Memorize it whole; the full form is explained at A2.

**Spoken forms:** سفر چطور بود؟ (unchanged), رفتم (unchanged), خسته نشدین؟ (*khaste nashodin?*), عکس گرفتین؟ (*aks gereftin?*). Notice that the past tense **changes far less** between written and spoken than the present — this unit's second gift.

grammars.title: Past stem + ending
body: The formula: drop ـن from the infinitive and attach the person ending. Example with رفتن ("to go"):
after: **Negative: the prefix نـ goes right before the stem.** رفتم → نرفتم (*naraftam*). Note the sound is **na-**, not *ne-* as in نمی.
**There's no می in the simple past.** رفتم, not می‌رفتم. (می‌رفتم does exist and means "I used to go" — the past continuous, an A2 topic.)
**Compound verbs:** only the verb part changes. کار کردم ("I worked"), خسته شدم ("I got tired"), گوش دادم ("I listened"), عکس گرفتم ("I took a picture").

grammars.title: Twenty verbs in the past tense
after: Compare this table with the present-stem table in unit 9. There, کردن had the stem کن and دیدن had بین — stems you had to memorize. Here they're simply کرد and دید, cut straight from the infinitive. That's the whole difference.

grammars.title: Past time expressions
after: **Both پیش and گذشته mean "last, ago"**, and both attach with ezafe: هفتهٔ پیش، سالِ گذشته. Spoken: هفتهٔ پیش → *hafte-ye pish* (unchanged), پارسال → *pârsâl*.

blocks.text: **"Did you have fun?" = خوش گذشت؟**, literally "did it pass well?". The standard question after anyone's trip, party, or weekend. The answer: بله، خیلی خوش گذشت ("yes, it was great").

blocks.title: Four linking words for telling a story
items: *avval* **اول** ("first") · *ba'd* **بعد** ("then") · *ba'd az ân* **بعد از آن** ("after that") · *âkharesh* **آخرش** ("in the end").
With these four words and the past tense, you can already tell about any day: اول رفتم بازار، بعد ناهار خوردم، بعد از آن به خانه برگشتم، آخرش خوابیدم. Try it tonight.

blocks.title: Persepolis (تختِ جمشید)
items: Its Persian name literally means "Throne of Jamshid", a mythical king in the شاهنامه. Its Greek name, *Persepolis*, means "city of the Persians". It was founded by Darius around 518 BC and burned by Alexander in 330 BC.

What remains still holds hundreds of carvings of envoys from twenty-three nations bearing tribute — each in the clothing and with the faces of their own land. Ten kilometers away, at نقشِ رستم, four royal tombs are carved into a cliff face.
Yesterday I went to the bazaar.

exercises.prompt: Change from the present tense to the past tense.
Fill in the right past-tense form.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: دیروز به بازار رفتم. — ما در رستوران غذا خوردیم. — او نیامد. — شما چه دیدید؟ — سفر عالی بود.
پنج‌شنبه با اتوبوس رفتم. — سفر چطور بود؟ — غذا تند نبود. — صبح رسیدم و مستقیم رفتم. — چهار ساعت آنجا ماندیم.
